- **Identity:** Stomp Under Foot La Scatola Nero octave-fuzz pedal.

La Scatola Nero is a fuzz pedal with an added octave function. Contemporary exact-model records identify it as an octave-fuzz design developed after a request from Ben McLeod of All Them Witches for a different fuzz with an octave added.

- Exact factory colorway sequence was not established from the sources reviewed.

- **La Scatola Nero:** exact cataloged model.
- Fuzz + octave architecture.
- No separately numbered factory revision established from the available exact-model records.

- No documented production revision split established.

- **Exact production transistor/device:** Not established in the available exact-model sources.

- **Exact clipping/rectification diode:** Not established in the available exact-model sources.

The model combines a fuzz voice with an added octave function, giving it a more aggressive upper-register texture than a conventional fuzz alone. Exact-model descriptions tie the concept directly to the request for a distinct fuzz with an octave function rather than simply transferring specifications from another Stomp Under Foot circuit.

Favourite Pedals by Preferred Pedal-Makers Dec 2, 2017 00:00 by  Stefan Karlsson Alexander Pedals Basic Audio Bearfoot FX Boss Catalinbread Chase Bliss Audio DigiTech Dr Scientist Dunlop Effects EarthQuaker Devices Effects Pedal Makers Electro-Harmonix Empress Effects Featured Foxpedal Fredric Effects Fulltone Effects Guitar Gear Retail Ibanez Jackson Audio JHS Pedals Keeley Engineering Kuro Custom Audio Mad Professor Effects Mooer Mu-Tron MXR OneControl Origin Effects Pigtronix Skreddy Pedals SolifGoldFX Spaceman Effects Stone Deaf Effects Strymon Subdecay Effects TC Electronic ThorpyFX VFE Pedals Wampler Xotic Effects Zvex + - Full Article Read Summary Key Points This directory lists favourite pedals by maker, alphabetical, covering over 2,000 pedals across more than 160 brands. It surveys major makers and models—Boss (Waza, 500 range, JB‑2), Chase Bliss (Tonal Recall, Warped Vinyl), Strymon (BigSky, TimeLine), Eventide (H9 Max), Empress (EchoSystem), OneControl/BJFE collaborations—and many boutique specialists and classic circuits (Analog.Man King of Tone, JHS, Electro‑Harmonix, MXR, Fulltone). The author prefers compact enclosures, maintains a dynamic wishlist, buys second‑hand if pristine, and weights tone, features, versatility, practicality, availability and price. Buffalo FX TD‑X is noted. As of March 2019, the price was £49. For electrical safety or to open/modify a pedal, consult a qualified tech. This essentially started as a companion piece to the previous / associated ’ More Pedal Chain Delight ’ article. I’ve since tagged on a whole heap of additional pedals which are of interest to me by those brands/makers already covered in my blog posts - these may or may not be universally acclaimed to be the best by said maker - they are purely my own preferences. I have a sort of ongoing dynamically adjusting wishlist where I log potential acquisition targets and weigh them up against everything else that is out there - in terms of tone, feature set, versatility, practicality, form-factor, availability and price. These things change on pretty much a daily basis - and are definitely highly influenced by price and availability as well as forthcoming pedal introductions. I am also very amenable to second-hand, as long as said pedals are in pretty pristine condition and as long as someone is not trying to fleece me at 2 or 3 times face-value.   The following listing is alphabetical by Pedal Maker Brand - with over 2,000 pedals covered across more than 160 key brands / makers.   Last updated March 2019. ADA Amps
